supporting_observations.claim: The supplied records show no PowerShell process creation or command line that would identify what caused the reported brief window.

At 13:44 UTC, the workstation downloaded about 38.8 MB through the proxy from download.windowsupdate.com using a Windows Update Agent user agent. This is consistent with update activity, but the records do not establish that it caused the reported window.

Google Drive File Stream started under maria.lopez’s account from Explorer, and its executable loaded a module recorded as signed by Google with a valid signature. Google Drive is not among the approved services in the supplied inventory; its presence is a policy concern but does not by itself establish malicious activity or data transfer.

A process recorded as svchost.exe accessed LSASS several times with granted-access values 0x1000 and 0x1400. The supplied records do not identify the hosted service or establish whether the access was malicious.
A short-lived conhost.exe process ran as SYSTEM with csrss.exe as its parent and exited shortly afterward. These records do not show that it hosted PowerShell or was the window reported by the user.

The file server resolved the workstation’s name and initiated a connection to its TCP port 135, but the recorded connection state is S2. These records do not establish successful remote administration or its purpose.
WmiPrvSE.exe processes were launched as SYSTEM with svchost.exe as parent. The available records do not show their activity or establish a link to PowerShell.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not include a PowerShell process event, command line, or script content; their absence here does not establish that PowerShell did not run.
The records do not provide a complete process tree or service mapping for the svchost.exe process that accessed LSASS.
The supplied WMI process-start events do not include WMI activity, command, or client details.
The file-server-to-workstation TCP 135 record does not establish a completed connection or the activity attempted.
The Google Drive process records do not show whether files were uploaded, downloaded, or synchronized.
claims_not_established: Whether a PowerShell window appeared on WS-MLOPEZ-01 during the reported time, and what process created it.
Whether any script or command ran, who initiated it, or whether it was authorized.
Whether the LSASS access or WMI activity was malicious or related to the reported window.
Whether Google Drive transferred organizational data.
Whether the file server’s TCP 135 connection attempt was related to remote administration.
additional_evidence_needed: Complete endpoint process-creation and process-tree telemetry for WS-MLOPEZ-01 around 13:20–14:20 UTC, including PowerShell and console-host events.
PowerShell Operational logs, including script-block and module logging where available, for the reviewed period.
Service and process details for the svchost.exe instance recorded accessing LSASS, plus endpoint security context for those accesses.
WMI-Activity logs and related client/process telemetry for the WmiPrvSE.exe launches.
FILE-HD-01 process, service, and network telemetry around 13:57 UTC to identify the purpose and outcome of its connection attempt to the workstation.
Proxy or endpoint transfer records for Google Drive File Stream to determine whether files were synchronized or transferred.
